name: osc-bridge
description: OSC ↔ MIDI/SysEx bridge for 981 synths and DAWs — a MIDI MCP and OSC MCP.
long_description: osc-bridge is a declarative bridge between OSC and the music world: 981 hardware synthesizers over MIDI/SysEx, plus music software over OSC (Ableton, Bitwig, Reaper, Sonic Pi, SuperCollider, Pure Data, TouchDesigner, VCV Rack). Its MCP server exposes the whole catalogue to an LLM — list devices, read a device's named OSC surface, send OSC to synths and DAWs, and check a running bridge's status. Both a MIDI MCP (hardware over MIDI/SysEx) and an OSC MCP (DAWs and live-coding environments).

default_target.title: Default OSC target
default_target.description: host:port that the send / get_status tools use when no target argument is given. Defaults to 127.0.0.1:7777 — the standard `osc-bridge run` bind.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: Find device drivers in the catalogue (about 981 synths, drum machines, controllers and DAWs). Without arguments it lists them all; `query` keeps drivers whose vendor, name or slug contain every word (e.g. 'korg minilogue'). Returns name, vendor, OSC prefix (slug), kind, source tier and firmware version when the source states one. Pass the slug to list_routes for the full CC/NRPN/SysEx map.

limit.description: Return at most this many drivers.

query.description: Words that must all appear in the vendor, name or slug (case-insensitive).

tools.name: get_device_docs
tools.description: Fetch the markdown companion documentation for one device, if present. The slug is the device's OSC prefix without the leading slash (e.g. 'ableton' for /ableton).

tools.name: list_routes
tools.description: Return the OSC routes a device exposes: declarative commands (OSC paths it accepts), cc/nrpn params, sysex params, named note triggers (drum sounds), and reply patterns. Use this to discover what a device can do.

tools.name: send
tools.description: Send a single OSC message to a running osc-bridge instance. Target defaults to the server's --default-target. Args are typed (int, float, string, bool).

args.description: Typed args. Each item is one of {int}, {float}, {string}, {bool}.

target.description: Optional override host:port (e.g. 127.0.0.1:7777). Defaults to MCP server's --default-target.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Send /bridge/status to a running osc-bridge and wait briefly for one reply per device (up to 500 ms).

tools.name: backup_presets
tools.description: Back up a hardware device's presets as a .syx file. Listens on the device's MIDI input and records every SysEx message it sends (a 'bulk dump'), stopping 3 s after the last one. Either the user starts the dump from the device's menu during the call, or pass request_hex (the device's dump-request message, from its manual or driver) with out_port. Use detect_hardware first to find the ports.

file.description: Path of the .syx file to write.

in_port.description: MIDI IN port of the device: index or name fragment (e.g. 'minilab').

out_port.description: MIDI OUT port for request_hex: index or name fragment.

request_hex.description: Optional dump-request SysEx as hex, e.g. 'F0 43 20 00 F7'.

tools.name: restore_presets
tools.description: Send a .syx file to a hardware device, e.g. to restore a preset backup. This OVERWRITES the device's memory: confirm with the user first, then pass confirm_overwrite: true. Messages are paced (gap_ms) because older devices drop fast dumps.

confirm_overwrite.description: Must be true: the user agreed to overwrite the device's memory.

file.description: Path of the .syx file to send.

out_port.description: MIDI OUT port of the device: index or name fragment.

tools.name: detect_hardware
tools.description: Find the MIDI devices plugged into this computer and match them to catalogue drivers. Lists MIDI ports, sends the standard MIDI Identity Request (harmless: it changes nothing on the device) and reads each device's manufacturer, model and firmware. Returns, per device, the best matching drivers and a ready-to-run 'osc-bridge run' command with the right port numbers.

probe.description: Send the Identity Request (default true). False only lists ports and matches by port name.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for identity replies, 100-5000 ms (default 800).
